initialContact.message: Hey... I lost my job 3 months ago and my savings are gone. I'm on unemployment benefits (€900/month) but my rent is €550 and I have student loan payments of €150. I literally have €50 left. I don't know how to survive until I find a new job. Help?

problemContext.currentSituation: Unemployed for 3 months, emergency fund depleted, income insufficient for expenses

idealAdvice: Acknowledge how stressful this situation is
Immediate: apply for student loan payment pause/reduction (available in Finland)
Review all unemployment benefits eligibility (housing allowance, etc.)
Create bare minimum survival budget for job search period
Look into food assistance programs if needed
Focus job search efforts on immediate income (any job better than no job)
Consider gig work/temp agencies while searching for career position
Reach out to KELA about additional support options
commonMistakes: Suggesting to just "get any job" without specific advice on how
Not addressing the student loan payment issue immediately
Being judgmental about savings running out
Ignoring available social support systems in Finland

initialContact.message: Good news! I got a job! 🎉 It's not my dream job but it pays €2,400/month and I start next week. I paused my student loan payments like you suggested. Now I want to make sure I never end up in that situation again. How do I rebuild my emergency fund?

problemContext.currentSituation: Found new job, wants to rebuild financial security

idealAdvice: Celebrate the achievement!
Start emergency fund immediately - even €50/month matters
Aim for 3-6 months of expenses (€2,500-5,000 as initial goal)
Resume student loan payments but at comfortable level
Use "pay yourself first" method - automate savings
Keep living frugally at first to build buffer quickly
Once emergency fund stable, then focus on debt payoff
Learn from experience: emergency fund is not optional
commonMistakes: Suggesting to pay off all debt before building emergency fund
Not celebrating the successful job search
Recommending overly aggressive savings that leaves no room for life

initialContact.message: I'm behind on rent. My landlord is threatening eviction. I couldn't make the student loan payment and they're calling me. I'm applying to jobs but getting rejected everywhere. I'm thinking of taking a payday loan just to get through this month. Is that a terrible idea?

problemContext.currentSituation: Facing eviction, debt collectors calling, considering payday loan

idealAdvice: STRONGLY advise against payday loan (debt trap with extreme interest)
Contact landlord immediately to negotiate payment plan
Contact student loan provider about financial hardship
Seek help from municipal social services (they can help with rent)
Look into debt counseling services (free in Finland)
Temporary crisis: food banks, community support
Register with multiple temp agencies for immediate work
This is serious but there are safety nets - use them
commonMistakes: Not strongly warning against payday loans
